commit_message:
lavc/dxvenc: improve compatibility with Resolume products

Improves compatibility with Resolume products by adding an additional
hashtable for DXT color+LUT combinations, and padding the DXT texture
dimensions to the next largest multiple of 16. Produces identical
packets to Resolume Alley in manual tests.

Signed-off-by: Emma Worley <emma@emma.gg>

fix_commit_message:
avcodec/dxvenc: Clear width to linesize not linesize to linesize

Fixes: use of uninitialized memory
Fixes: 422217206/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_AV_CODEC_ID_DXV_fuzzer-4786889444098048

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix a45755e302ba on top of intro d4556c98f02e via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (UninitializedMemory): In libavcodec/dxvenc.c, the DXV encoder pads frames whose width or height is not a multiple of 16 into a newly allocated buffer (safe_data) before running texture compression. When padding the width dimension, the code zeroes out the padding region using an offset/length derived from frame->linesize[0] (the original frame's row stride) instead of the actual pixel-data width in bytes. Since linesize can differ from (and is generally larger than) the tight pixel-data width, this causes the memset to target the wrong byte range within each row of the newly allocated, non-zero-initialized buffer, leaving part of the true padding area uninitialized. This uninitialized memory is later read by the texture compression routines and encoded into the output DXV packet, resulting in a use-of-uninitialized-memory bug (and potential leak of heap contents) detected by fuzzing under MemorySanitizer. Root cause: The fix commit's boundary calculation for clearing the padded encode buffer used the frame's linesize (row stride) as a stand-in for the row's real pixel-data width, but these are not necessarily equal; linesize can already contain padding independent of the DXV_ALIGN requirement. This mismatch between 'stride' and 'true data width' let a region of freshly allocated (uninitialized) memory escape being zeroed.
